# eu-gpai-code-of-practice-safety-security-measure-3-5
- **URL:** https://code-of-practice.ai/?section=safety-security ("EU AI Act: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice · Final Version", full text) and the summary at https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/code-of-practice-overview/ (both raw HTML via curl) · **Accessed:** 2026-09-16 · **For:** v2→v3 response round, slice K (K7)
- **What it establishes:** In the Code's Safety and Security chapter, Measure 3.5 is titled "Post-market monitoring" (not "independent external evaluators"); it contains the external-evaluator ACCESS commitment. The duty to have external evaluators CONDUCT model evaluations is Appendix 3.5 "Independent external model evaluations". The Code speaks in "Signatories will" (a voluntary code); the artificialintelligenceact.eu overview paraphrases this as "shall"/"must" and is NOT the official wording.
- **Key passages (final-version text):**
  - Measure 3.5: "To facilitate post-market monitoring, Signatories will provide an adequate number of independent external evaluators with adequate free access to: the model's most capable model version(s) with regard to the systemic risk that is made available on the market; the chains-of-thought of the model version(s) in point (1), if available; and the model version(s) ... with the fewest safety mitigations implemented with regard to the systemic risk (such as the helpful-only model version, if it exists) ... unless the model is considered a similarly safe or safer model ... Such access to a model may be provided by Signatories through an API, on-premise access (including transport), access via Signatory-provided hardware or by making the model parameters publicly available for download, as appropriate."
  - "Signatories will publish suitable criteria for assessing applications." · "Signatories will not take any legal or technical retaliation against the independent external evaluators as a consequence of their testing and/or publication of findings as long as the evaluators: do not intentionally disrupt model availability ...".
  - Measure 3.5 monitoring methods include "implementing privacy-preserving logging and metadata analysis techniques of the model's inputs and outputs using, e.g. watermarks, metadata, and/or other at least state-of-the-art provenance techniques".
  - Appendix 3.5: "In addition to internal model evaluations, Signatories will ensure that adequately qualified independent external evaluators conduct model evaluations pursuant to this Appendix 3, with regards to the systemic risk, unless: the model is a similarly safe or safer model pursuant to Appendix 2; or Signatories fail to appoint adequately qualified independent external evaluators, despite using early search efforts (such as through a public call open for 20 business days) and promptly notifying identified evaluators, in which case Signatories will take into account the potential additional uncertainty arising from the absence of independent external evaluations".
  - Appendix 3.4: "a period of at least 20 business days is appropriate for most systemic risks and model evaluation methods".
  - Overview-site paraphrase (do not quote as the Code): "Signatories shall provide sufficient numbers of independent external evaluators with complimentary access to the model's most advanced versions, including variants with minimal safety constraints".
- **Reliability:** code-of-practice.ai is an unofficial reader site reproducing the final (July 2025) text; the Commission PDF itself was not opened. Wording should be checked against the Commission PDF before print if quoted at length.
- **Relevance to this project:** The evaluators are selected and appointed by the provider, with an escape hatch if none can be found; note Measure 3.5 also lists input/output logging as a monitoring method (relevant to the essay's layer-3 concern).
